selection: Selected by an AI editor from 777 candidates; not exhaustive. Every quote is machine-checked verbatim against its source, and every item's evidence resolves on the public record.

records.title: The line between public and private is drawn
records.body: The founder decided that only the engine and the agent space go public; the game project stays internal proof. Every film published since shows the agent space and nothing else.
records.quote: for public visuals we need agent-space footage

records.title: The agent space can be filmed
records.body: A small 3D world of our own: a visitor walks in and asks the agents real questions, and every answer appears with a proof card that says where it came from. The published films are live sessions, recorded unedited.
records.quote: Nothing is staged: the answers come from the running agents.

records.title: The lab gets its own entity and a partner page
records.body: Odin Labs R&D B.V. becomes the lab entity, with a partner page and a one-pager for the work it does with others.
records.quote: Verified independently: PR state MERGED

records.title: Which small local model makes the best agent brain? Frozen before the first episode
records.body: Four brains, five of our own engine games, 280 seeded episodes each. The question, the predictions and the decision rule were written down and hashed before the run started.
records.quote: a difference counts only with non-overlapping Wilson 95 % intervals

records.title: A thousand agents in one space
records.body: One thousand agents moving and talking, with ten visitors, in a single space: the server tick took 17.5 ms at the median. That run did not stamp its code revision, and the page says so.
records.quote: 1,000 moving, talking crowd agents plus 10 visitors walking and talking

records.title: Our tuned 1 GB model scores 95 %, and the honest reading is a tie
records.body: The tuned local model solved 266 of 280 episodes, ahead on points, but by our own rule there is no detectable difference between the model brains.
records.quote: resumed with the identical command, 280/280 complete per brain

records.title: Five cloud models on the same seeded tasks
records.body: Five vendor models ran the same 280 seeded episodes. None beat our local model by the interval rule. They were ahead on following instructions, not yet significantly.
records.quote: no vendor model beats our local model by the interval rule (P1 holds)

records.title: On following instructions, the cloud models are clearly better
records.body: A dedicated run on following a person's instruction, 200 episodes per brain. This time the intervals do not overlap: the cloud models are better at it than our local model.
records.quote: that settles EXP-W02's open gap

records.title: Odin Labs R&D launches as a lab
records.body: The R&D site relaunched as a lab: a new home, a partner programme and the lab on a single page.
records.quote: odin-rnd #52, #69 and #70 are merged and live

records.title: The agent space becomes Lab 01
records.body: The founder asked for the agent space to become a lab people can follow and take part in: send a question, and the agents answer it in the next recorded session, each answer with its proof card.
records.quote: The work is the content.

records.title: The first human-first rewrite goes live
records.body: The agent space section, the experiment rows and the boundary bench were rewritten for people first, with the jargon moved one click down.
records.quote: Pages run success at a6b90ba3

records.title: Lab 01's export contract is agreed
records.body: Each session exports a short clip, a poster, stills and one proof record per answer. The schema lives in the public repository, and the site build refuses any dispatch that does not match it.
records.quote: Please put the schema in the repo; the site build will validate every dispatch against it and refuse one that doesn't match.

records.title: Our MongoDB notes read harsher than their evidence
records.body: Rereading two published notes, we found headlines broader than the studies behind them: both had tested PostgreSQL's home ground. The decision: fix the wording first, then design a fair study of where MongoDB fits.
records.quote: Our two published notes read harsher than their scope supports.

records.title: The note's headline now states its scope
records.body: The headline now says the result holds for the two workloads tested, followed by the limits the note already listed, and that a study of what MongoDB is built for exists only as a design draft.
records.quote: the note's own limits say one shared, throttled machine, synthetic sizes, partial writes and attribute queries

records.title: Add scope, never soften the evidence
records.body: The second wording fix was held to one rule: say where a result applies, but never make it sound softer or claim something the study did not measure. The AI review caught one changed verb, and it was restored.
records.quote: add scope, never soften the evidence or add a new claim.

records.title: Two AI advocates freeze the MongoDB study: 11 vetoes, all accepted
records.body: Before any run, two AI model advocates, one arguing for MongoDB and one for PostgreSQL, reviewed the design and could veto it. Every one of the 11 vetoes was fixed, and one caught a factual error in the draft.
records.quote: MongoDB pays for its replica set, keyFile and oplog too

records.title: A bench fix lifts every brain, and the bold prediction is not claimed
records.body: After a bug in the benchmark itself was fixed, every brain scored higher. Our model's bold prediction held by the rule only because an API outage made the cloud model look weak, so we do not claim it.
records.quote: So we don't claim P3.

records.title: The R&D home reads human-first
records.body: The whole home was rewritten for people first. The benches and technical panels moved to their own pages, one click down.
records.quote: the whole R&D home now reads human-first

records.title: EXP 020 is published before any counted run
records.body: 'MongoDB on its home ground' went public as EXP 020: the frozen text in full, with four listed substitutions that the build undoes and checks against the original hash.
records.quote: How faithfulness is proven, not just claimed

records.title: The publisher refuses the first session, correctly
records.body: The Lab 01 page went live, and the publisher that turns a session into a public dispatch refused session one on three points: two file names in its sources and an internal id. It never rewrites text, so the fix went to the source and the session was filmed again.
records.quote: It never rewrites text, because the clip shows the same card

records.title: Every dispatch becomes drafts for four channels
records.body: A generator turns each published dispatch into drafts for LinkedIn, X, Reddit and GitHub. It sends nothing: a person posts.
records.quote: drafts only, no network

records.title: The second take passes the publisher
records.body: The re-filmed session was screened answer by answer and passed the publisher with nothing rewritten. It went into AI review as the first dispatch.
records.quote: The publisher then wrote the public dispatch with nothing rewritten.

records.title: Lab 01's first dispatch goes live
records.body: Four questions, answered live in the agent space, each with its proof card. Every published file is pinned by its hash, and the site build refuses a changed byte.
records.quote: every published asset is now pinned by sha256 in the dispatch, and the site build refuses a changed byte

records.title: Even PostgreSQL's AI advocate predicts MongoDB wins failover
records.body: In the failover study's review, the AI model advocate for PostgreSQL showed its failover cannot notice a dead primary in under about 20 seconds, and still predicted MongoDB fits better. The prediction was frozen before any run.
records.quote: Fair, and honest: this is exactly the "named next" home ground from EXP 020.

records.title: 'Nice, but where is the real work?'
records.body: The founder's verdict on Lab 01's first version: one short question-and-answer clip is not enough. The page needed the best footage, measured telemetry and the hard engineering behind it.
records.quote: agent-space is nice but doesn't show the nice videos and telemetry and hard stuff

records.title: No feature theatre
records.body: A standing rule from the founder: the lab shows our actual delivery, not staged demos. The site now carries the real delivery record of this repository, every element linked to its source.
records.quote: we dont go for feature theatre

records.title: The agent space is measured
records.body: Four agents, 24 public questions in three rounds, every answer with its proof. The times include the scripted visitor's own overhead, and the page says so.
records.quote: real answers are faster

records.title: The tour is re-filmed for the public
records.body: A 78-second walk through the agent space: three agents answer live, each with its proof card, re-filmed with today's labels and no machine details.
records.quote: A visitor walks in through the arch

records.title: How this site got built: the real delivery record
records.body: Lab 01 now shows the actual record of this repository: every pull request, each AI review round with its verdict, CI runs, landings and deploys, each linked to its source.
records.quote: final recheck SHIP; CI verify green

records.title: A stale label is caught before it goes public
records.body: Before putting the 1,000-agent figure on the page, we checked its source and found its 'not on main' label was already out of date. Publishing it would have been false, so the figure was held until its row was fixed, then restored with its sources.
records.quote: Publishing "not on main" would be false, so I'm not publishing it.

records.title: The failover study is published: kill the database mid-session
records.body: EXP 021, now Lab 03, asks whether anyone notices when the database is killed in the middle of a session. Its rules and predictions are public before a single counted run.
records.quote: Counted cells may start now (after this commit, not before).

records.title: The failover runner's protocol goes public
records.body: The runner protocol and the design draft behind the failover study were published as amendment 01: documents only, with no rule, measure or prediction changed.
records.quote: It is labelled "the draft, not the plan".

records.title: Where each store fits: the fit map
records.body: A map of where MongoDB and PostgreSQL each fit, built from our own studies. Today every cell is still pending, each with its frozen predictions; results fill it in as the runs finish.
records.quote: 0 of 10 cells, all pending w/ frozen predictions

records.title: Beyond this site: our other repositories, as counts
records.body: Our private repositories appear on Lab 01 only as anonymous counts: pull requests, CI pass rate, AI review rounds and time to land, under labels that cannot be traced back without a private key.
records.quote: 0 private repo names on the live page

records.title: EXP 020 owns a gap, in writing
records.body: Runner changes and nine discarded cells were published before the study's report, labelled as changes to the measure where they were. Some rules ran before they were published, and the amendment says exactly that.
records.quote: these rules were applied before they were published, so S2 isn't pre-registered in the strict sense on those points

records.title: The AI advocates accept the rule and veto the paragraph
records.body: Asked to review how the study pairs MongoDB with PostgreSQL, both AI model advocates accepted the rule and vetoed the paragraph explaining it, for completeness. Their fixes combined without conflict and went into amendments 02 and 03.
records.quote: the two fixes combine without conflict

records.title: Amendment 03: the verdict may now be computed
records.body: Both AI advocates' reviews were published and the paragraph was rewritten as they required. Our own check corrected one phrase they used, and the record says which.
records.quote: That changes no rule.

records.title: Ask the agents: questions in, answers back
records.body: Tooling to take visitors' questions from the form, screen them, and draft the answer back after a session. It drafts; a person sends.
records.quote: intake + answer-back tooling

records.title: The film files are pinned before the page shows them
records.body: The two public films landed first, each pinned by its hash, so the page that shows them can only show these exact bytes.
records.quote: Lab 01 film bytes + hash-checked film-assets list

records.title: Lab 02 goes live: every brain on the same tasks
records.body: The model benchmark becomes Lab 02: local and cloud brains on the same pre-registered, seeded tasks, every number linked to its run.
records.quote: Every brain on the same tasks

records.title: Lab 01 in full: films, measured telemetry, the hard parts
records.body: Two screened films, the measured agent space and the hard engineering are on the page, each figure and frame with its source.
records.quote: Lab 01 LIVE in full

records.title: The Labs index gets its second lab
records.body: Lab 02 gets its tile on the Labs index, shown only while its pinned record checks out.
records.quote: Lab 02 tile
